title: Enhancing LLM-based Quantum Code Generation with Multi-Agent Optimization and Quantum Error Correction
problem: LLM-based quantum code generation struggles with fault-tolerance and correctness; general-purpose LLM techniques (CoT, RAG) don't translate to quantum domain without domain-specific optimization.
motivation: Quantum programming is emerging as critical infrastructure, but quantum error correction and circuit optimization are domain-specific challenges that generic code generation frameworks cannot adequately address.
method: The system uses multiple specialized AI agents, each focused on a specific quantum optimization: error correction (fixing quantum computational errors) or circuit synthesis (designing efficient quantum circuits). A semantic analyzer—a component that understands code meaning—runs multiple passes to refine the results, applying Chain-of-Thought reasoning (where the AI thinks step-by-step) alongside an error correction decoder to catch and fix quantum mistakes. Testing measures each agent's contribution.
key_novelty: Multiple AI agents, each specializing in a different quantum code optimization like error correction or circuit design, work together in one framework.
contributions: Multi-agent architecture with specialized agents for quantum optimizations
Semantic analyzer with multi-pass inference for quantum program verification
Error correction code decoder integrated into generation pipeline
Structured CoT improves quantum algorithm accuracy by 50%; error prediction/correction demonstrated
limitations: Evaluation on limited quantum benchmark set; scalability to large quantum circuits and gate decompositions not discussed.
primary_theme: Quantum-specific multi-agent LLM code generation with error correction
